Both s1 and s2 directly call the module-level checkToken function as their if condition; its definition is at f1:205.

The upload branches are inside the positive if checkToken(...) bodies at s1 and s2, without a negation or comparison to a constant. The helper returns True on a successful request and False on an exception (f1:211–215).

checkToken supplies the candidate token as an Authorization header and returns success or failure according to whether its remote request raises an exception (f1:205–215). This tests the outcome of a server request.

The missing-artifact checks return before token collection, and positive validation permits uploadToken in both collection paths (s3–s6). uploadToken sends the collected data through LoadUrlib (f1:292), so these checks enable exfiltration.

The collection functions proceed when the target artifacts exist and upload candidates when checkToken succeeds (s3–s6). These decisions activate collection on available target data rather than detect an analysis environment.

The existence checks require the source directory or decryption state before reading token data (f1:399–406, f1:472–484). checkToken then checks whether a recovered credential works before it is uploaded, supporting data_availability.

Regions s5 and s6 follow their respective artifact early returns and lie inside the positive validation branches. Following the unresolved remainder resolves uploadToken at f1:411/f1:488 to its definition at f1:216, then LoadUrlib at f1:292 to f1:88 and the network call at s7.

The same LoadUrlib sink is also reached from upload, including its kiwi branch at f1:328. The module calls upload('kiwi', ...) at f1:681 without requiring either token-validation branch, so s7 is not exclusive to this gate.

The returns at f1:415 and f1:445 guard the following bodies in their respective functions; the SQLite query at f1:422 sits directly in s3.
The query at f1:422 is inside getPassw after its existence-check return, so every invocation must pass that gate. The thread target at f1:550 enters the same guarded function and provides no bypass.
sql_connect is imported from sqlite3 at f1:7, and f1:419-423 copies the login database, opens it and queries username and password fields. This sink reads stored credentials.

The loginusers.vdf check applies only inside the Steam elif branch at f1:501-510, while s11 also runs for wallet and browser arguments that skip that branch. Thus c3 alone can reach s11, contradicting the conjunction and minimum of two conditions.

s10 follows the Steam file-check return and s11 follows the directory-check return in ZipThings. The call at f1:515 resolves to upload, whose f1:390 call resolves to LoadRequests and its file POST at f1:83.
GatherAll also calls upload directly for password and cookie report files at f1:569-570, bypassing both ZipThings guards. That call reaches the same LoadRequests file POST through f1:331 and f1:390.

upload opens the archive argument as a binary file at f1:330-331 and passes it to LoadRequests at f1:390. The requests import at f1:39 resolves the f1:83 POST to a network API that transmits those file contents.
Each region follows its cited file-check return or lies inside its cited file or directory branch. The call in s24 resolves to uploadToAnonfiles in s25, which contains the network sink s23.

The only calls to uploadToAnonfiles are f1:589 and f1:603, respectively after the file-check return at f1:586 and inside the file-check branch at f1:602. The directory branch reaches KiwiFolder at f1:607, whose upload call still passes its own file gate.

uploadToAnonfiles opens the selected local file in binary mode at f1:573 and supplies it as the files argument to requests.post at f1:574. The requests binding is imported at f1:39, establishing a network sink that sends file contents.
The condition at f1:502 directly negates os.path.isfile and returns when it is false; os is imported at f1:4.
The early return at f1:502 permits the read only when loginusers.vdf is a file. The Steam entry at f1:538 supplies the claimed directory to ZipThings through f1:564, and pathC retains that directory.
The test checks whether the Steam loginusers.vdf artifact exists before opening and reading it, which fits target_artifact.

The regions at f1:409 and f1:486 follow their respective path checks and successful checkToken decisions. The cited call at f1:411 reaches uploadToken, its LoadUrlib call at f1:292, and the network sink at f1:92.

The same LoadUrlib sink is also reached from upload at f1:328, f1:360 and f1:389. GatherAll calls upload at f1:570 without requiring either checkToken decision, so the sink is not exclusive to the cited gate.
uploadToken includes the token and account data in the serialized data passed to LoadUrlib at f1:292. Its sink at f1:92 uses urllib.request.urlopen and Request, imported at f1:12, to send that data.
The return at f1:496 guards the process call, archive upload and deletion in f1:497-516. The upload call reaches upload at f1:299, then LoadRequests at f1:390 and its file POST at f1:83.

Although the process and deletion sites are inside ZipThings after its guard, GatherAll also calls upload directly for password and cookie files at f1:569-570. That route reaches LoadRequests and the same f1:83 network sink without the f1:496 gate.

subprocess.Popen at f1:497 creates a process, and os.remove at f1:516 deletes the archive. upload opens the archive at f1:331 and passes it through LoadRequests to requests.post at f1:83, supporting exfiltration.

Reaching f1:503-510 requires passing both the pathC existence return at f1:496 and the nested loginusers.vdf file check at f1:502. Those two cited conditions therefore combine with AND and have a minimum of two.
Failure of either existence check returns before the Steam file read, while passing both enables the open and read at f1:503-504. This fits enables.
The checks continue when the target data directory and Steam login file are present, allowing that file to be read. This is activation on available target artifacts.
The checks verify the directory and login file immediately needed by the following open and read operations. That supports data_availability.
The open call at f1:503 lies inside the cited f1:503-510 region and follows both early returns at f1:496 and f1:502. It is directly in the region, so an empty witness is sufficient.

The cited open at f1:503 occurs only in the Steam arm of ZipThings after both existence checks. Both thread entry sites at f1:562 and f1:564 enter the function before those checks and cannot bypass them to reach this sink.

The built-in open imported at f1:2 opens loginusers.vdf in r+ mode at f1:503, and f1:504 reads its lines. The following scan inspects the remembered-password setting, supporting the claimed credential artifact read.
